rulings.verbatim: Mac is the prove-and-build substrate. Full stop. NO paid infra without explicit founder sign-off. Free tier only (Oracle Always Free, GitHub-hosted runners, etc.). If it costs >EUR 0, it waits until after prove-and-build is done. Real cluster follows proof, never precedes it. Exceptions: none until further notice.
rulings.meaning: This laptop IS the production substrate until the founder says otherwise. Zero-cost only: GitHub-hosted runners, free tiers, and local clusters (k3d/k3s on this machine). Any proposal for a paid resource -- a rented node, a managed cluster, a paid tier, a provider invoice -- is REFUSED with 'Founder ruling R14: Mac substrate only', not escalated and not re-explained. A session that has already asked does not ask again in different words. PROOF COMES FIRST AND THE CLUSTER FOLLOWS IT: manifests, policies and drills are proved locally, and only a completed proof can justify reopening the spend question. Reverses the standing shape of crew#78, which was asking for a rented box before anything had ever been applied to a cluster.
rulings.enforced_by: rule-guard.py PreToolUse refuses a command that provisions or pays for infrastructure (hcloud/doctl/aws/gcloud/az create, fly deploy, terraform apply against a paid provider); crew#78 is marked blocked on this ruling so the ask stops regenerating

rulings.verbatim: first of all the macbook must never sleep, we need to prove everything works locally first, we dont want local to diverge from prod, no ruling stays everything working in laptop first
rulings.meaning: TWO PARTS, both binding. (1) THE MACBOOK NEVER SLEEPS. Under R14 this laptop IS production, so a sleep is a production outage, not a power setting. It is enforced by the OS itself -- 'sudo pmset -c sleep 0 disksleep 0 standby 0 powernap 0' -- and never by a caffeinate process under a KeepAlive LaunchAgent. caffeinate is a userland assertion: it is a no-op for system sleep on battery, it dies with the login session, and it is exactly the hand-rolled wrapper over a real OS setting that R6 bans. Measured 2026-08-24: com.founder.estate-awake reported PID alive and LastExitStatus 0 while the machine entered sleep 6 times on AC power that same morning. A session that finds a sleep in 'pmset -g log' treats it as an incident and routes it, with that log line as the receipt. The machine being on battery is the same outage arriving later; say so the moment you see it. (2) LOCAL IS THE REFERENCE, AND IT MUST NOT DIVERGE. Everything is proved working on this laptop before it is claimed anywhere else. There is no 'works in CI' and no 'works on the remote' -- a component that only runs after a manual step, only runs in a workflow, or only runs on a box that is not this one has not been proved. When local and any other environment disagree, that gap is the defect and the local side is the reference. This sharpens R14: R14 said the Mac is the substrate; R15 says a divergence from it is a bug you fix, not a difference you document.

rulings.verbatim: Command guards are Rego under policy/. Python guards are deprecated and rejected by CI.
rulings.meaning: A refusal that can be decided from the command string is an entry in policy/command.rego with its `re`, `marker`, `msg` and the `must_match`/`must_not_match` examples that keep it honest. `make guard NAME=x` scaffolds one and the test fails until real examples replace the TODOs. Do not add a `def rule_` to rule-guard.py: the count is ratcheted and CI refuses a rise. The six that remain shell out to git or gh to ask about the live tree, which Rego cannot do; they are the backlog, not the pattern. Numbered R16 because R15 was taken by the laptop-never-sleeps ruling while this branch was open. Enacted by the cutover in PR #28, which moved nine refusals after replaying 35,705 commands through both implementations with zero disagreements.
rulings.enforced_by: policy/hand_rolled_policy.rego (rule_ceiling, policy_dir_py, legacy line ceilings), gated by .github/workflows/policy.yml

rulings.verbatim: ok good job but alway research, it pays off all the tine
rulings.meaning: Before choosing any tool, standard, protocol or version, search the current state of the world and cite what you read. Not memory, not what the training data believed, not what another session asserted. The incident that paid for it: on 2026-08-24 a session started building an ingress on Traefik's own Docker labels. Research showed two things it did not know -- Kubernetes SIG Network retired the ingress-nginx controller on 2026-03-24, and Gateway API core is GA at v1.6.0 with 16 conformant implementations. The real decision was the config language, not the vendor: routes written as HTTPRoute are portable, routes written as vendor labels are not. Research changed the answer, and it cost one search. This is LAW 43 with a due date: the research is online, it is the agent's job, and it goes on the record with the sources named.
rulings.enforced_by: idp and crew: every ADR carries a Sources section with dated URLs; adr-sources-guard.py refuses a decision record that cites nothing

rulings.verbatim: also we have oracle free tier now, so we are ready, but firt we need to verify local env and prepare for the big one, add topersistent board notes or anywhere agets will refresh asap
rulings.meaning:
An Oracle Cloud Always Free tenancy now exists. It is the destination for the k8s migration (crew#78). It does not conflict with R14 zero-cost (free tier is free; R14 blocked PAID infra) nor R1 (Fly-specific).

STEP 1 IS A PROOF, NOT A COMPLAINT. 'Verify local env' means: run the WHOLE workload on the current substrate -- compose estate + k3d + Dagster + all 40 schedules -- and prove every part RECONCILES CORRECTLY. Reconciles means converges to desired state. Slow is a measurement; wrong is a failure. The proof requires everything UP at once, so stopping a component to make the machine comfortable destroys the proof rather than advancing it.

THE ARGUMENT THIS BUYS, AND THE ONE IT FORBIDS. With the proof in hand the Oracle case is 'the Mac cannot SCALE' -- correct behaviour, measured cost, headroom exhausted. Without it the only available case is 'the Mac is broken', which is a weak argument that reads as an operator who cannot run their own machine, and which a buyer's engineer takes apart in one sitting. Never argue the migration from breakage, throttling or an outage. Argue it from a green proof plus a ceiling.

ORDER: (1) prove the full workload reconciles, (2) prepare, (3) move. Nobody provisions Oracle capacity, creates a cluster or points anything at it until step 1 is proved with commands. 'We are ready' means the BLOCKER is gone, not start cutting over. R15 stands: the laptop is the substrate until the migration actually happens.
rulings.enforced_by: none yet -- procedural. Recorded on crew#78 as the premise change.
rulings.verbatim_followup: "Local green" does not mean "add more to the Mac." It means "prove the compose estate + k3d + Dagster + 40 schedules all reconcile correctly on the current substrate." Once that proof is in, the case for Oracle is that the Mac cannot scale, not that it is broken.

rulings.verbatim: Every container image in the estate must support both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. No exceptions. No per-environment hacks. One image tag, two architectures, runtime picks automatically.
rulings.meaning: Every image the estate pushes is a single tag carrying a linux/amd64 and a linux/arm64 manifest, built by `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64` in GitHub Actions and pushed to GHCR. The Mac (x86_64) pulls amd64, OKE (Ampere) pulls arm64, nobody configures anything. Local builds go through idp/bin/build-image; CI blocks a single-arch push.
rulings.enforced_by: idp/bin/build-image (refuses a single --platform), idp/bin/multiarch-gate (every build-push-action and docker build call must name both platforms; fixtures both ways in idp-ci), idp/.github/workflows/build-multiarch.yml, STANDARDS.md row.

rulings.verbatim: we need this operational estate wide plain ... Every PR must update the BDD scenario or the auto-gen script. If the PR changes code but not the executable spec, the CI blocks merge. No manual doc updates. No 'I'll update the wiki later.' ... alert peers
rulings.meaning: Documentation that lives outside the execution path rots. Three mechanisms are the estate rule: (1) BDD scenarios are the spec and the test, so a PR that changes code must also change a .feature file or the generator that produces the live diagram; CI blocks it otherwise. (2) Diagrams are generated from live state (launchd, docker, the catalog), never drawn by hand. rulings.verbatim: you need to be clear and make things easy and intuitive, i miss too many things i need to do, if something depends on me and is blocking, it needs to be loud, visible and super friction free for me to act, law
rulings.meaning: When a step depends on the founder (a sign-in, an approval, a decision), the session (1) sends a PushNotification the moment it blocks, (2) states in the reply, above the fold, one line starting FOUNDER ACTION: with the exact URL, button or word he must give and where the tab is, (3) leaves nothing else for him to read or find. Never bury the ask under evidence, never pipe the prompt's URL into a log he cannot see, never say 'the tab should be open'. A blocked ask he did not see is the session's failure, not his.

rulings.verbatim: Stop thinking about prospector. Prospector is one customer. I want the research engine that prospector calls. The engine is the platform. Prospector is just a user.
rulings.meaning: The capability is an autonomous research engine. Five behaviours are proved before any scheduler, tracker or eval tool is touched: (1) question generation: 100 dossiers in, 10 unasked hypotheses out; (2) experiment design from one hypothesis: test, data, method; (3) execution and recording with no human; (4) calibration: Brier score against outcomes, published; (5) explanation: what it learned and why it changed its mind, one sentence. Tool choice is the cheapest that lets the five run; cost is optimised after. Sharpens R28.

rulings.verbatim: why are we concerned with the old dossiers when we want to exponentially improve things, old dossiers were duck taped together, our new capabilities should be sneering at this and want to prove they can generate much better ideas for all scales
rulings.meaning: The research engine is not fed, tuned to, or measured against the old prospector dossiers. It generates its own ideas from scratch, at every scale (one company, one market, the estate). The old corpus has one use: a baseline the engine must beat, shown side by side. Any plan whose first step is 'load the old dossiers' is the old system wearing a new name. Sharpens R31.

rulings.verbatim: ok lets adopt this but every 30 minutes not 4 hours ... and ensure everyone is permanently doing this without me asking ... this way even if agent sessions die, we can recover easily
rulings.meaning: Every session appends a handoff to ~/.estate/feed.md at least every 30 minutes: six lines at most, each starting with 🔴 Blocked / 🟡 Active / 🟢 Done / ⚪ Pending / 📍 State. The feed is the persistent brain; a session that dies has left its state there. A session that starts with 'Status' reads the feed and summarises it; nobody re-explains and the founder is never asked what the feed already says. Enforced by ~/.claude/scripts/feed-guard.py on Stop (blocks an overdue turn), SessionStart (injects the last entries) and UserPromptSubmit (reminder). Append with: python3 ~/.claude/scripts/feed-guard.py append --session <id> --lane <repo>.

rulings.verbatim: We are changing our approach entirely. ... we are officially banning the words "refactor," "rewrite," or "update" regarding the engine. ... every claim carries its source in an append-only, object-locked bucket ... every forecast is Brier-scored ... a Golden Corpus of 50-100 hand-researched dossiers is the oracle.
rulings.meaning: The research engine is net-new, not a cleanup of the old one. Every claim names a locked source (R2 object lock, append-only); every forecast is logged and Brier-scored (MLflow); the science plane is Argo/MLflow/Kubernetes; differential replay against the old engine is dead; a 50-100 item Golden Corpus, crew-researched online from existing dossier titles, is the oracle; the buyer sees a calibration curve. Full text: crew docs/rulings/R34-net-new-research-paradigm-verifiable-calibrated.md.

rulings.meaning: The research/science/ML capability is a platform layer in idp, on the same row as model routing and traces. rulings.verbatim: Research is a crew. Science/ML is a layer. ... Research discovers what to build. Science predicts when it will be ready, if it will break, and whether the founder can be interrupted. Both are mandatory. Neither can wait. ... a Python 'tapeworm' script writing to a local SQLite database on your Mac is completely incompatible with the elite, cloud-agnostic standard we just established. ... it must be impossible for any potential data point to be missed.
rulings.meaning: Research looks outward (markets, competitors, capabilities) and is a crew whose adoption decisions end with the founder's last call. Science/ML looks inward (sessions, CI, guards, budget, founder response) and is an embedded layer, always on, no opt-out: OTel Collector on the cluster, ClickHouse, MLflow + Langfuse, Brier-graded predictions, founder as calibration authority. Three controls, all proven tools: (1) admission - a Kyverno ClusterPolicy (Enforce) refuses any provider annotation, StorageClass, CSI driver, LoadBalancer class or second secret door outside the declared provisioner boundary (platform/oci, platform/secret-store, clusters/<name>), and the same policy judges every rendered PR before the cluster sees it; (2) continuous proof - the whole Flux tree hydrates on a second provider (k3s on a non-Oracle VM) on every PR that touches platform/ or clusters/, and that run is a required status check on main; (3) the control is written as a control (docs/policy/provider-independence.md) with rule, boundary, enforcement points, evidence query and owner. rulings.verbatim: also i hope all platforn nigration is autonated , idenpotent and portable . tents all peers nust verify  ... Every tool migration (whether adding a service, upgrading a database schema, or switching an orchestrator) must satisfy five non-negotiable criteria
rulings.meaning: THE ESTATE MIGRATION STANDARD. Every migration -- adding a service, changing a schema, swapping an orchestrator -- satisfies five criteria, runs through three phases, and is enforced in CI. FIVE LAWS. (1) IDEMPOTENT: running it once or a hundred times leaves the same state, with no error and no duplicate resource. (2) ZERO UNINTENDED SIDE EFFECTS: migrating component A never drops a volume, kills an unrelated port, or edits a global config outside A's boundary. (3) REVERSIBLE: every forward step has an equivalent undo that has been run, not just written. (4) AUDITABLE: each migration event records who ran it, when, the git commit SHA, the previous state and a verification hash. (5) DOCUMENTATION FIRST: first-time setup may be manual, but it emits a structured runbook BEFORE any automation is written. THREE PHASES. Phase 1 Discovery/Spike: fiddly work allowed, local sandbox or temp branch ONLY, output is a raw runbook capturing every env var, port, volume and config. Phase 2 Codification: turn the runbook into automation with four entry points -- a pre-check (can_apply), an apply, a healthcheck, and a rollback. Phase 3 GitOps: the pipeline applies it. No manual SSH, no ad-hoc docker run, and successful validation writes to ESTATE_STATE.md programmatically. ENFORCEMENT ON AGENTS, because agents reach for docker volume rm and untracked curl. A migration ticket cannot be closed without the script path and a dry-run log attached. A PR that introduces a new service binary or container with no up/down/healthcheck lifecycle script FAILS CI. The state ledger is written by the automation, never by hand. AND: all peers must verify. A migration is not done because the session that wrote it says so.

rulings.verbatim: final decision
rulings.meaning: Said immediately after the founder's own analysis that undocumented ports are how backdoors are created and that Backstage, not a PORTS.md, is the ledger. It closes the routing and identity questions together. (a) ROUTING: as already recorded in idp ADR 0001, routing is Gateway API; services are addressed by name; no service publishes a host port; no routing rule is written in a vendor's own syntax. Front door Traefik, agent-to-tool traffic agentgateway -- a different layer, deliberately not the front door. (b) BIND POLICY: the gateway is the ONLY process that binds a non-loopback address. Everything else binds 127.0.0.1 or nothing. Measured 2026-08-24: 18 of 25 binds were already loopback; the two violations that are ours are the Backstage backend on *:7107 and the k3d API forward on *:53145. (c) IDENTITY, the question ADR 0001 left open and the founder had to ask twice: identity is OIDC, enforcement is at the gateway via Envoy ext_authz (Gateway API GEP-1494 HTTPExtAuthFilter, Experimental -- written as Traefik ForwardAuth until it lands), and the implementation is Authelia. No application keeps its own login. Keycloak is not rejected on merit; it is an IdP and not a proxy, so it needs oauth2-proxy plus a JVM plus a Postgres where Authelia is one Go binary doing both -- and because the contract is OIDC, swapping to it later changes an issuer URL, not a route. Zitadel is AGPL-3.0 and we are selling this platform. (d) The registry of endpoints is the Backstage catalog entity, never a hand-maintained PORTS.md (LAW 28). Recorded in idp/docs/decisions/0003-identity-is-oidc-and-the-gateway-enforces-it.md.

rulings.verbatim: also backstge call this nachine production, this is dev not prod. ens dev, stage prod  /  we need envs setup across platfron, we nust be env aware
rulings.meaning: THREE ENVIRONMENTS ESTATE-WIDE: dev, stage, prod. Every tool, catalog entity, config, secret path and deployment is environment-aware, and no file hardcodes which one it is (LAW 46). THIS LAPTOP IS dev. It is not production and nothing may label it production. The incident: idp/bin/catalog-gen line 97 wrote a literal 'lifecycle: production' onto every component, so the developer portal told anyone who opened it that a laptop was the production estate -- wrong, and wrong in the direction that makes a reader relaxed. Fixed 2026-08-24 in idp commit b68bc52. RESOLUTION ORDER, use this everywhere: $ESTATE_ENV, then the first line of ~/.estate/env, then 'dev'. The fallback is dev on purpose -- if the environment cannot be established, the safe default is the one that makes you careful. An unrecognised value EXITS, it never guesses. Backstage mapping: spec.lifecycle uses Backstage's own vocabulary (experimental for dev and stage, production for prod); the precise estate env is carried as an annotation, which is what machine-driven things key off.

rulings.verbatim: you must eliminate trust. If a system relies on an agent, engineer, or script 'doing the right thing,' it will fail. Guarantees come from mechanical friction -- hard automated gates that make failure physically impossible to merge or execute.
rulings.meaning: FIVE MECHANISMS. This is how R19 is enforced rather than hoped for. 1. DOUBLE-RUN + ROLLBACK CI GATE. Never take an agent's word that a migration is idempotent. CI proves it in three phases on a pristine temporary environment: apply (health check passes), apply AGAIN on the same running environment (exit 0, and a diff showing zero state mutations and no duplicate resources), then rollback (environment returns to its exact pre-migration state). Any phase fails, the PR fails. 2. MACHINE-ATTESTED STATE LEDGER. Agents are FORBIDDEN from hand-editing status text in ESTATE_STATE.md. A binary runs real healthcheck assertions, compiles HTTP status codes, latency and row counts, signs the payload and auto-commits the table. To claim a service is live you make it pass the probe; you do not edit a file. This is R16 made mechanical. 3. GITOPS RECONCILIATION. Actual state must equal git state. A reconciliation loop pulls desired state from main on a schedule; anything created out of band by a manual docker run, kubectl edit or port change is reverted to the manifest. 4. SCHEMA-ENFORCED CATALOG AND PORT LOCK. Every service repo carries a catalog-info.yaml against a strict schema declaring name, domain, assigned port block and dependsOn. CI fails instantly if a container binds a port not registered in its catalog entity, or if two services claim the same port. Peer session chidionyema-1d shipped the first half of this on 2026-08-24: idp#16 and estate#2, 25 ports as catalog Resources, catalog-gen exits 3 on a double-claimed port, proved both ways in idp-ci. 5. MANIFEST-FIRST AGENT EXECUTION. Agents emit a job manifest (action, name, image, ports, migration script, health endpoint) rather than running raw shell on the primary machine. A deterministic host runner validates it against security rules, runs it sandboxed, verifies the health endpoint, and only then applies. This is what stops docker volume rm and global pip install. ||| AMENDMENT, founder ruling same day, ratifying chidionyema-a6's design: MECHANISM 2 IS TWO-TIER, PER ROW, AND EACH ROW PRINTS ITS CLASS. The original wording said the ledger is 'signed'. That claim cannot be honoured on this machine: every agent runs as uid 501 with the same filesystem access, so a key the signer can read is a key the graded party can read. An on-box signing key is theatre and must not be built. [ATTESTED] = the GitHub Actions runner took the reading itself. Tamper-proof, because the laptop never supplies the number. Rows: uv lock --check, catalog schema validity, decision record exists, mkdocs.yml exists, CI conclusion, image digests, licence scan, bin/port-gate static. [TAMPER-EVIDENT] = a local probe on this host took the reading. Append-only: a false reading is possible, a quiet retraction is not. Rows: container up, HTTP probe, bound sockets, launchd job fired, bin/port-gate --live. CI RE-MEASURES, IT DOES NOT RE-SIGN. A signature over a payload the laptop committed attests that the workflow signed it, not that it is true; an agent that can push can get a false claim signed. Signing is cosign keyless via Actions OIDC (Fulcio cert bound to the workflow identity, Rekor log) so there is no key on the box at all. REJECTED: a macOS Keychain item with a code-signed-binary ACL -- real friction, but macOS-only, which breaks LAW 34, and it dies when the binary is rebuilt. A GATE THAT GRADES PROSE IN A PR BODY IS [TAMPER-EVIDENT], NEVER [ATTESTED] -- the author supplied the paragraph. The class goes in the row's own output, never as a caveat at the bottom of the file, because a caveat at the bottom is the thing everyone stops reading. Tracked: crew#190, five CPs. VOCABULARY: the environments are dev, stage, prod. 'staging' is an alias resolving to stage, not a fourth name (R21, and bin/catalog-gen already enforces it).

rulings.verbatim: no 2 tier, Backstage only
rulings.meaning: BACKSTAGE IS THE SINGLE SURFACE, AND THE CATALOG IS THE LEDGER. Said while R22 mechanism 2 was being built as a two-tier ESTATE_STATE.md -- rows marked [ATTESTED] where a CI runner took the reading itself, [TAMPER-EVIDENT] where only the laptop can see it. The ruling does not reject that trust boundary; it rejects the file. ESTATE_STATE.md is not the surface at all, so making it defensible was making a redundant thing sturdier. State is an entity's annotations and its health, read from the portal. FORBIDDEN: do not build bin/attest-state, do not build the append-only store, do not split ESTATE_STATE.md rows into two tiers, and do not stand up a second surface for status, tickets or catalog. crew#190 is closed on this ruling. WHAT SURVIVES, because none of it was about the markdown file: CI re-measures rather than trusting a number the laptop supplied, now applied to whatever the catalog reads. No on-box signing key -- every agent runs as uid 501, so a key the signer can read the graded party can read too. bin/port-gate and bin/bind-audit are untouched: they already write to the catalog rather than to a table in a file, which is exactly why this ruling does not reach them. crew#186 keeps mechanisms 1, 3, 4 and 5; mechanism 2 is now 'the catalog is the ledger'. THE SECOND HALF. He asked in the same breath where his tickets are and where his UI surface is, and the honest answer was that they are in two places and he was told about neither. So 'Backstage only' also means the crew GitHub issues must reach him through a surface he can open, not a third board. Interim per R24: the free GitHub Projects board. Portal-native later via @backstage-community/plugin-github-issues v1.3.1 and @backstage-community/plugin-github-pull-requests-board v1.3.1, both Apache-2.0, both published 2026-08-21; idp's app-config.yaml already carries an integrations.github block waiting for a token, and that token needs the sops vault R21 calls for, which does not exist yet.

rulings.verbatim: The k8s cluster is currently WIP across multiple lanes. It will be the final destination in a day or two, but you need forward motion right now to manage the dependency catalog. We cannot wait 48 hours to have a working Backstage, but we also cannot accept the brittle yarn start laptop hack.
rulings.meaning: BRIDGE ARCHITECTURE, TWO PHASES, AND THE INTERIM MUST BE THE SAME ARTEFACT AS THE FINAL. PHASE 1, TODAY: Backstage runs from its official Docker container via a lightweight interim docker-compose.yml. Not `yarn start`. The reason is not tidiness -- a container is the same artefact k8s will run, it enforces the port bindings rather than inheriting the host's, and it isolates the app from the laptop. That gives a live catalog today so dependency mapping can start now. PHASE 2, AFTER THE CLUSTER IS GREEN AND SIGNED OFF: the SAME image gets Kustomize manifests, ArgoCD is pointed at them and syncs Backstage into the cluster, and the interim container is deleted. ArgoCD takes over Backstage deployment only after the cluster is finalised -- not before, and the cluster is finalised when the founder says so (R17). THE RULE THIS GENERALISES TO: an interim step is acceptable when it is the same artefact as the destination and its removal is one delete. `yarn start` fails that test and a container passes it. Do not offer an interim that has to be unpicked. TICKETS: the free GitHub Projects board is the interim UI so he has a surface today; it does not reopen the ONE BOARD ruling, because crew GitHub Issues remain the single store and Projects is a view of them. Kanboard stays retired.
